SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitation helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATION
Study Imitation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various

What this means
In this part you learn to respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Imitation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Imitation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

2. why people communicate 2) When do you speak to communication in different  Learners listen to and practice them?
3. Why do you speak to b) use appropriate vocabulary to  Learners simulate communication them?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various.
